Rosenbaum's p-value for the exact adaptive test

Source: R/rosenbaum-pairs.R
riposte_adaptive_smallest_level.Rd

The smallest level alpha at which the adaptive test, with its cutoffs chosen by conditions (4)-(6) of Rosenbaum (2012), rejects the observed counts. Rosenbaum defines the test's p-value this way: "The P-value ... for the adaptive test is the smallest alpha in (4)-(6) that leads to rejection" (p. 100). Because the cutoffs are chosen separately at each level, this number can fall at or below a level more often than that level allows when there is no effect: with 11 untied pairs at gamma = 1, it is at most 16/256 with chance 20/256. riposte_adaptive_pvalue() gives a p-value that keeps its level, and riposte_test() prints both.

Usage

riposte_adaptive_smallest_level(y, gamma = 1, lambda = c(1/3, 2/3))

Arguments

y

matched-pair differences (treated minus control). Zero differences are dropped. Ties among |y| are broken by order (ties.method = "first") with a warning, because the paper assumes untied ranks.

gamma

sensitivity parameter.

lambda

the two band fractions 0 < lambda[1] < lambda[2] <= 1 (default c(1/3, 2/3)).

Value

the smallest rejecting level, in (0, 1]; 1 when no level below 1 rejects.

References

Rosenbaum, P. R. (2012) An exact adaptive test with superior design sensitivity in an observational study of treatments for ovarian cancer. Annals of Applied Statistics 6(1), 83-105.
